public_comment.topic: An architect (former board member) proposed a zoning change letting open-air front porches encroach 8 to 10 feet into the 40-foot front setback; board members were receptive and asked him to return at the next meeting.

A board member asked whether a change to the water supply for the O'Brien development would require modifying the planning board's permit; the planner said it would likely be a modification reopening the public hearing process.

budget_items.what_was_said: The committee reported the engineers' renovation estimate was revised down after being questioned, and members doubted renovation would be accepted by Town Meeting given tear-down and rebuild costs are close.

decisions.decision: The front porch setback proposal will be put on the next meeting's agenda for discussion with the architect.
Parking table to be cleaned up and brought back at the next meeting for a final vote so it can go on the spring Town Meeting warrant, which closes in mid-March.
Board preferred to pursue zoning articles at the spring Town Meeting rather than a special town meeting.
Hotel/hospital/B&B parking to be changed back to one space per employee on the largest shift, like other uses; multifamily 1.5 spaces to be combined into two per unit.
Child care parking to be one space per employee on the largest shift plus one per five children, dropping the lower rate over 20 children.
Planner will resend the subdivision definitions as a PDF the next morning after a mismatched digital copy was found.
Next meeting March 8 will hold the site plan approval rules hearing, followed by a North End Subaru hearing.

minutes.headline: Planning Board reworked subdivision and parking rules for the spring Town Meeting warrant; no substantive votes taken.
minutes.summary: The board heard a proposal to let front porches extend into the front setback, got an update on a second Green Leaf Botanicals community meeting, and worked through subdivision definitions and parking requirements. It agreed to bring a cleaned-up parking table back for a final vote next meeting, aiming for the spring Town Meeting. Only minutes approval and adjournment were voted.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board took no substantive votes; only the February 8 minutes and adjournment were voted.
The board agreed to bring a cleaned-up parking table back at the next meeting for a final vote, so it can go on the spring Town Meeting warrant.
Members preferred to pursue the zoning articles at the spring Town Meeting rather than a special town meeting.
Parking changes discussed included child care, hotel and multifamily rates; subdivision definitions will be resent as a PDF after a mismatched copy was found.
A former board member proposed letting open-air front porches extend into the front setback; it goes on the next agenda for discussion with the architect.

why_it_matters: The parking table and subdivision rules are zoning changes that could be put to voters as articles at spring Town Meeting, so what the board settles in March sets what residents are asked to vote on.
Porch setback, parking and subdivision changes affect what can be built on residential lots and how much parking developments must provide.
watch_next: March 8 meeting: site plan approval rules hearing, then a North End Subaru hearing, with the parking table due back for a final vote.
The spring Town Meeting warrant, which closes in mid-March.
